7.text: Anthropic’s amended IPO filing shows Q3 revenue near $17 billion (up 47%) but a $567 million operating loss and $895 billion in compute commitments, with spending outpacing revenue. Investors Michael Burry and Jeffrey Gundlach question its growth assumptions and debt prospects, while its cloud suppliers—including Alphabet’s Google—sell the compute Anthropic depends on.

19.text: Google launched a Universal Cart for AI shopping and opened AI Mode in Search to service-business integrations like Jobber; Tessell released Gemini-based database agents on Google Cloud. Other items cover Hightouch, Ideavo, a set-top-box botnet takedown, Bluehost, Presentations.AI, Apple/Siri, and SpeedyIndex, bearing on Alphabet only marginally.

14.text: Google is building a $17B, 702-MW Wyoming data center powered by Bloom Energy fuel cells and buying Crusoe's troubled Wyoming project, plus backing TeraWulf's ~$19B Anthropic leases in Kentucky. Separately, PSEG plans a 200-MW nuclear uprate, Xcel faces pushback on Google's 780-MW Project Skyway, and Google says demand will exceed its data center supply.

6.text: Alphabet missed Q3 earnings and revenue estimates, with per-share profits down 26% year-over-year and free cash flow negative due to $51.4B in AI infrastructure capex, triggering its worst single-day stock drop (~10-11%). Despite this, articles cite accelerating Google Cloud revenue, strong search query growth, and a cheap valuation as reasons to buy the selloff.

15.text: Market research reports forecast growth in edge computing, next-gen computing, quantum computing, SMB IT spending, and small language models, profiling Google among key players. Other articles cover AI code assistant growth and Journify's $12M raise, with no direct Alphabet developments.

16.text: Alphabet raised its SpaceX stake by nearly 4 million shares, bringing the holding to roughly $69 billion, though its board representative resigned after 11 years. SpaceX’s AI compute business now exceeds half its revenue, and a Google data-center energy executive cautioned that space-based data centers can cost far more than Earth-based ones.

4.text: Amazon and Microsoft reported record cloud growth and margins alongside rising AI capex, with AWS capacity selling out and Microsoft's Azure accelerating; markets debated whether profits can keep pace with spending. Alphabet appears only as edging higher in one rally, so the articles bear on it mainly as hyperscaler peer context.

18.text: Presentations.AI added Google Docs-to-Slides conversion and a free Chrome extension. Reddit will test limiting Google search visibility outside the U.S., and a study found prediction markets in half of sampled Google midterm forecast searches.
